items.title: R.C.H. Smith Interview, 1975-10-02
items.q: I did have a chance to play with Earl Father Hines in San Francisco.

ctx.x: Who else did you hear live other than Horry's band? Who else did you hear? Who else did you hear?

In Los Angeles in those days, there was a guy named Pete Daly out of Chicago-style Dixieland band. He was quite good. Clareness, Rosie McHarg. It's a long time since I really thought about those people. I never was fond of playing that way. I found myself in New York in the 50s, 50 to 55, playing alongside an incredible roster of musicians. This was in the days with the Conrad Janus band. Conrad Janus on the Tailgate Five, he called it. It was a five-piece group usually. But we'd play alongside just about the…
What else? Could you tell me that story again about Zutty? About Zutty? If that's worth telling again. Oh, I...

items.title: R.C.H. Smith Interview, 1975-10-02
items.q: finally I worked my way back to uh some Louis Armstrong and the Hot Five and Hot Seven things like that really liked those

ctx.x: Well, that would be good for a trumpet player. You know, you get the Howard in there.

Some people like that. Let's talk about Kid Ory. Kid Ory, to me, now we're premising this on the fact that I did play in his band on his pickup gigs and on weekends during the period of about 1958 through 1960. Maybe there was some in 57. I don't know. I recall the George Lewis band at that time, though, in San Francisco. But my early recollections were Ory on Records, of course, those wonderful crescents that came out of Los Angeles, swinging things with Mutt Carey and Bud Scott, and then as I got in college, I…
Did he have a theme song then, really?
